text:
ara: Heads-up — thinking about a refactor to make the intake pipeline more modular. Rough goal: split lightweight admission (fast checks) from heavy validation (bench, quant tests). Want quick feedback before I draft an RFC.

mike: +1 on separation. main question: sync vs async for heavy checks?

julia: can we keep the converter deterministic? if converter outputs change we blow up bench diffs.

sam: agree w/ julia. also curious about surface area of the contract. minimal is better.

ara: proposal: two simple contract shapes: `admit_v1` (fast metadata) and `bench_report_v1` (async results). Keep admit_v1 tiny so gateway can decide quickly.

mike: do you have a sketch?

ara: sketch of admit payload:
```json
{
  "admit_v1": {
    "model_id": "string",
    "files": [{"name":"model.bin","sha256":"..."}],
    "flavors": ["llama","gpt2"],
    "runtime_hints": {"seq_hint": 1024, "kv_cache": true},
    "fingerprint": "hex"
  }
}
```

julia: good. add a small `capabilities` array for feature flags (tool calling, streaming) so downstream routing can pick the right runtime.

ara: yep, I was thinking `capabilities": ["tool_calling","streaming","structured_output"]`

sam: tradeoff note: if we allow fast admit we reduce time-to-serve but risk surface regressions. maybe `admit` can include a `recheck_required` boolean and a `partial_admit` state.

mike: for heavy bench — run async workers and post to `/admit/results/{model_id}` with a `bench_report_v1` payload. If bench fails, we set `status: gated` or `blocked`.

bench-bot: notify: bench job queued for model 'm-2026-03' (job id 7071) :gear:

julia: fallback policy? if async bench errors, default to `partial_admit` with strict canary throttles, not full production.

sam: yep. Another option is to allow `admit` with `time_window` (how long a partial admit is allowed before it must be rechecked).

ara: suggested status state machine in RFC: `blocked` -> `admitted` -> `partial_admit` -> `gated`. Each admit payload carries `status` and `schema_version`.

mike: also include `fingerprint` as deterministic matching across stages (converter/runtime/bench). makes dedup and cache hits easier.

julia: we should version the schema (admit.v1 then v2). keep backward compat: extra fields are optional.

sam: ops question: how do we treat function-calling or tooling tests? as capability bits in the admit so routing chooses a runtime that supports them.

ara: exact. we treat them as capability flags.

mike: bench infra note: bench run should sample multiple batch sizes and provide a small profile (p50/p95) and a link to artifact. store the artifact in the model namespace.

kevin: infra implications: queue sizing, TTLs for partial admits, and a small k8s job pool. we'll need a backpressure plan if intake spikes.

sam: timeline?

ara: I'll draft the RFC with the state diagram and example messages by EOD tomorrow. Julia will prototype a gateway patch that emits `admit_v1` for new uploads. Kevin to size infra. Prototype in ~2w, canary after sizing.

bench-bot: notify: bench job 7071 completed — latency 12.3ms p50, 45ms p95, status PASS

julia: sweet, can we attach a smoke artifact link?

bench-bot: artifact: https://artifacts.redwood/7071/smoke.json

ara: will include artifact references and recheck TTLs in the RFC. thanks all — tagging @kevin for infra follow-ups.

mike: 👍

sam: sounds good.

julia: will drop the gateway prototype PR today.

kevin: noted, will run queue estimates and follow up with infra cost/limits.

ara: thanks everyone — RFC incoming.
